entities.name: Celtic Arena Bestiary — Running Notes
entities.tags: Celtic, arena bestiary, lore, running notes
entities.summary: GM guidance for running Celtic Sphere arena bouts: tone, useful terrain, negotiable creatures, ready-made bouts, and the collection's Krea image prompt.
entities.body:
Celtic arena creatures should feel wild, beautiful, treacherous, and deeply tied to old boundaries: a road, a ford, a burial mound, a hearth, or the edge of the woods. Standards create pressure; Elites bring a trick or condition; Bosses refresh Spark Shield at half Flesh and unleash their phase break. Telegraph those turns with green mist, a ringing hoofbeat, a sudden tide, or a name whispered by the crowd.

**Useful terrain:** standing stones, thorn hedges, black-water pools, peat bogs, moonlit moors, burial cairns, and ruined roundhouses.

Many are negotiable. A Glaistig may honor protection, a Púca may leave after a clever joke, and an Each-Uisge may be hungry rather than loyal to its handler.

## Ready Bouts

**The Drowned Ford:** Kelpie and Each-Uisge compete for victims as the arena slowly floods through broken standing stones.

**Three Barks Before Dawn:** Cù Sìth Green Hound with Black Shuck and Cait Sìth among moonlit cairns.

**Headless Procession:** Dullahan leads Redcaps through a thorn maze while champions race to stop the naming ritual.

**The Fomorian Claim:** Fomorian Tide-Brute attacks a coastal arena defended by Glaistig and the Boar of Ben Bulben.

## Krea 2 Turbo Prompt

A dark fantasy Celtic mythic creature collection inside Asterion, a towering arena city built from the broken Tower of Babylon: a black Púca shapechanger, a dripping Kelpie water horse, a huge green Cù Sìth hound, spectral Black Shuck, screaming Banshee beside a broken cairn, headless Dullahan rider on a black horse, scaled Each-Uisge marsh horse, red-capped iron gremlins, horned Glaistig keeper, one-eyed Fomorian tide brute, ash-black Cait Sìth cat, and enormous bristled Boar of Ben Bulben. Separate torch-lit stone, thorn hedge and black-water arena pens, standing stones, peat mist, moonlight, rain and crowded shadowed stands. Palette of deep moss green, wet black, moon silver, old gold and ember red; richly detailed painterly dark fantasy creature concept art, grounded mythic anatomy, no modern objects, no text, no watermark.

entities.name: Slavic Arena Bestiary — Running Notes
entities.tags: Slavic, arena bestiary, lore, running notes
entities.summary: GM guidance for running Slavic Sphere arena bouts: tone, useful terrain, investigation hooks, ready-made bouts, and the collection's Krea image prompt.
entities.body:
Slavic creatures bring folktale dread into Asterion: deep woods growing through stone, flooded mills, hearth spirits, grave hunger, impossible birds, and death hidden outside the body. Standards add fast hazards, Elites twist terrain or impose conditions, and Bosses refresh their Spark Shield at half Flesh before their phase break. Telegraph it with a crow’s call, a snapping birch branch, a furnace flare, or water rising through the floor.

**Useful terrain:** birch groves, crooked cottages, waterwheels, grave markers, oven doors, thorn fields, ash drifts, and frozen ponds.

Several creatures reward investigation: Koschei’s soul-token, a Domovoi’s household taboo, or a Leshy’s lost path can end a bout without pure force.

## Ready Bouts

**The Mill Below:** Vodyanoy Mill-Predator and Rusalka Reed-Singer as floodgates turn the arena into a black-water maze.

**Three Heads, One Storm:** Zmey Gorynych in a ring of burning birches that change the breath weapon’s danger.

**House That Walks:** Baba Yaga Bone-Hen, Kikimora swarm, and Domovoi sprites defend a shifting cottage arena.

**Death Outside the Body:** Koschei Bone-Fragment commands Upyr Grave-Eaters while champions search for the hidden soul-token.

## Krea 2 Turbo Prompt

A dark fantasy Slavic mythic creature collection inside Asterion, a towering arena city built from the broken Tower of Babylon: a massive three-headed Zmey Gorynych dragon breathing fire frost and lightning, antlered Leshy grove-haunter, pale Rusalka river spirit, mossy Vodyanoy mill predator, tiny Kikimora thread crawlers, iron-beaked Baba Yaga bone-hen, ash-covered Domovoi sprite, gaunt Upyr grave-eater, radiant Alkonost sorrow-bird, blazing Firebird, horned black Chort ravager, and skeletal Koschei bone-fragment carrying a needle blade. Separate torch-lit wood, stone, graveyard and flooded-mill arena pens, birch trees, crooked ovens, runic stones, ash, fog and crowded shadowed stands. Palette of ember orange, birch white, deep violet, swamp green, black iron and old gold; richly detailed painterly dark fantasy creature concept art, grounded mythic anatomy, no modern objects, no text, no watermark.

entities.name: Indic Arena Bestiary — Running Notes
entities.tags: Indic Sphere, arena bestiary, GM guidance
entities.summary: Running guidance, terrain, notable exceptions, ready bouts, and the full-collection art prompt for the Indic arena bestiary.
entities.body:
## Running Indic Beasts
Indic bouts should carry cosmic scale without reducing sacred traditions to decoration: celestial rivers, lotus courts, storm clouds, temple carvings, forest canopies, and the tension between preservation, transformation, and disorder. Standards keep the arena moving, Elites control perception and positioning, and Bosses refresh Spark Shield at half Flesh before their phase break. Telegraph that escalation with bells, monsoon winds, lotus petals burning, a mantra becoming audible, or a serpent shedding its skin.

**Useful terrain:** river ghats, lotus pools, temple gates, banyan roots, cloud bridges, mountain shrines, mirrored halls, and rain-slick stone.

Creatures are not automatically evil. Garuda may demand justice, a Kinnara can test artistic worth, and a Naga may defend a sacred water source against reckless intruders.

## Ready Arena Bouts
**Monsoon Gate:** Makara River-Lion and Naga of the Thousand Steps turn a rain-channel arena into a rising flood.

**The Mirror Court:** Rakshasa Mirror-Eater and Vetala Corpse-Whisperer confuse challengers amid reflected torchlight and ancestor niches.

**War Beneath the Cloud Bridge:** Asura Iron-Heart faces Garuda Sun-Raptor and Vanara Rooftop Raiders across collapsing high walkways.

**The Poisoned Lotus:** Kaliya Venom Wyrm commands Pisacha Ash-Ghouls while Gandharva Cloud-Stag offers a path to escape.

## Image Generation Prompt (Full Collection)
A dark fantasy Indic mythic creature collection inside Asterion, a towering arena city built from the broken Tower of Babylon: a jeweled Naga serpent, mirror-faced Rakshasa, massive Makara river-lion, golden Garuda sun-raptor, corpse-haunting Vetala, armored Asura warrior, musical Kinnara archer, stone-carved Yali temple beast, ash-covered Pisacha ghoul, agile Vanara raider, cloud-antlered Gandharva stag, and black venom Kaliya wyrm. Separate lotus-pool, temple-stone, cloud-bridge and banyan-root arena pens, monsoon rain, braziers, carved gates and crowded shadowed stands. Palette of saffron gold, lotus pink, deep indigo, river jade, rain gray and ember orange; richly detailed painterly dark fantasy creature concept art, grounded mythic anatomy, no modern objects, no text, no watermark.

entities.body:
## Running Eastern Beasts
This collection combines creatures from Chinese and Japanese mythic traditions, matching the setting’s combined Sino-Japanese sphere. Their bouts emphasize foxfire deception, weather, waterways, dream logic, sacred judgment, and colossal horror. Standards are quick support threats; Elites challenge focused champions; Bosses refresh Spark Shield and trigger their phase break at half Flesh.

**Useful terrain:** jade bridges, lantern courts, canal pools, tiled rooftops, paper wards, bamboo screens, thunder drums, and cloud platforms.

Creature motives matter: Qilin may refuse cruelty, Baku can be bargained with for nightmares, and a Kitsune’s “defeat” may only be an elaborate test.

## Ready Arena Bouts
**Lantern Court Masquerade:** Nine-Tailed Fox against a team navigating false exits, foxfire clones, and shifting masks.

**Storm Over Jade:** Long River Dragon Spawn and Tengu Storm-Kite across suspended bridges as monsoon water rises.

**Canal of the Hungry Dead:** Kappa Canal Wrestler, Jiangshi Bell-Hoppers, and a Gashadokuro Bone Giant behind the final gate.

**The Dream Verdict:** Baku Dream-Eater and Qilin of the Jade Trial; violence is allowed, but mercy changes the reward.

## Image Generation Prompt (Full Collection)
A dark fantasy Sino-Japanese mythic creature collection inside Asterion, a towering arena city built from the broken Tower of Babylon: a jade Qilin, nine-tailed fox surrounded by blue foxfire, hopping Jiangshi corpse, massive red Oni with iron club, tiny Kitsune shadow-pups, winged Tengu storm-kite, elephantine Baku dream-eater, turtle-backed Kappa canal wrestler, coiling Long river dragon with a lightning pearl, chimera Nue on a tiled roof, wise white Bai Ze beast, and colossal skeletal Gashadokuro. Separate jade, black stone, lacquered wood and bronze arena pens; lanterns, paper wards, canals, cloud platforms, rain and stormlight; crowded shadowed stands. Palette of jade green, lacquer red, moon white, midnight blue, antique gold; richly detailed painterly dark fantasy creature concept art, grounded mythic anatomy, no modern objects, no text, no watermark.

### The Sun in Motion

**Domains:** Sun, war, conquest

Militant, uncompromising, and expansionist; he seeks victory through struggle and forward motion.

## Asterion Seat

Solar Advance: Move up to 30 ft in a straight line and make a 2-damage strike; if it hits, allies may each advance 10 ft.

## Mythic Deed

Dawn Won by Struggle: Once per session, break a major stalemate through decisive action: scatter a besieging force, seize the vital objective, or ignite courage in a collapsing army.

Work That Cannot Be Denied: Once per session, finish an impossible labor under pressure: breach a fortress, build an escape, repair vital infrastructure, or arm a resistance.

Honeyed Accord: End hostility between two willing parties for one scene; each gains +1d10 on a cooperative action.

River of Reconciliation: Once per session, turn a bitter rivalry toward genuine renewal, restoring bonds and resources only if both sides honor a public, equitable exchange.

entities.name: Mesoamerican Arena Bestiary — Running Notes
entities.summary: Guidance for running Mesoamerican arena bouts, useful terrain, ready-made encounter hooks, and the collection's image-generation prompt.
entities.body:
Twelve sun-fed, rain-soaked, obsidian-toothed, and star-haunted creatures for arena spectacle.

Mesoamerican bouts should feel ceremonial and elemental: pyramid platforms, obsidian mirrors, rain channels, solar fire, starless eclipses, and the terrible pressure of an old cosmic order. Standards harry the field, Elites control mobility and sightlines, and Bosses refresh their Spark Shield at half Flesh before their phase break. Telegraph escalation with drumbeats, falling ash, a dimming sun, rising rain, or a carved calendar stone cracking open.

**Useful terrain:** stepped pyramids, ballcourts, cenote water, obsidian mirrors, jungle roots, jade braziers, feather banners, and sacrificial stone platforms.

Creatures need not be simple monsters. The Feathered Serpent may judge a champion, Coyote may bargain for a secret, and an Ahuizotl might seek the return of something stolen from its water.

## Ready Arena Bouts

**Black Sun Ballcourt:** Tzitzimitl Star-Demon and Jaguar of the Obsidian Night hunt champions as eclipse shadows spread.

**Rain Against Fire:** Tlaloc Rain-Toad swarm and Xiuhcoatl Fire Serpent turn a stepped temple arena into steam and burning stone.

**The Cenote Opens:** Cipactli River Maw and Ahuizotl Hand-Tailed Hunter attack as water rises through the floor.

**Feathers of the Last Sky:** Feathered Serpent confronts Camazotz Cave-Bat and an Ocēlōtl War-Eagle above broken pyramid platforms.

## Image Generation Prompt (Full Roster)

A dark fantasy Mesoamerican mythic creature collection inside Asterion, a towering arena city built from the broken Tower of Babylon: a majestic feathered serpent flying above steps, skeletal Tzitzimitl star-demon, black jaguar with obsidian claws, turquoise Xiuhcoatl fire serpent, enormous crocodilian Cipactli river maw, hand-tailed Ahuizotl water hunter, huge Camazotz cave-bat, sly Coyote trickster, bone-white Xolotl hound, rain-covered Tlaloc toad swarm, ghostly Cihuateteo crossroads wraith, and armored Ocēlōtl war-eagle. Separate obsidian, jade, red stone and cenote-water arena pens; stepped pyramids, feather banners, rain, solar fire, jungle roots and crowded shadowed stands. entities.name: Yoruba Arena Bestiary — Running Notes
entities.summary: Guidance for running Yoruba arena bouts, useful terrain, ready-made encounter hooks, and the collection's image-generation prompt.
entities.body:
Twelve river-born, iron-clawed, ancestor-haunted, and crossroads-touched arena creatures.

These creatures bring rivers, ancestral presence, iron, thunder, forest paths, and the unpredictability of crossroads into Asterion’s arena bouts. Standards create fast pressure, Elites control movement or perception, and Bosses refresh Spark Shield at half Flesh before their phase break. Telegraph that moment with drumbeats, iron ringing, sudden rain, swirling masquerade cloth, or a path opening where there was no path.

**Useful terrain:** red-earth courts, river channels, iron forges, sacred groves, drum circles, shrine gates, masks, and branching crossroads.

Some creatures can be bargained with or redirected: the Eégún answers ritual respect, the Esu goat changes sides for the right offer, and an Iwin may lead a champion out rather than kill them.

## Ready Arena Bouts

**Crossroads of Iron:** Esu Crossroads Goat and Ogun Forge-Hyena transform the field with swapped positions and weapon hazards.

**Ancestor Drum:** Eégún Ancestor Masquerade commands an Aje Night Crow Swarm beneath a storm of ritual cloth and drumbeats.

**Red River Trial:** Àjàpá River Serpent, Omi River Hippopotamus, and Iku Ash-Crocodile battle as floodgates open.

**Hunt on the Sacred Road:** Leopard of the Iron Road pursues Iwin Forest Antelope through a shrinking grove arena.

**The Gilded Court.** Allies must publicly name a bond or duty; enemies who break a declared promise become Weakened.

entities.name: Greek Arena Bestiary — Running Notes
entities.summary: GM guidance for running Greek arena bouts, useful terrain, and ready-made bout hooks for the Olympian sphere bestiary.
entities.body:
Greek bouts are heroic trials made lethal: cracked temples, bronze statuary, black springs, labyrinth walls, and bright marble under an uncaring crowd. Standards pressure the field, Elites impose one defining complication, and Bosses refresh their Spark Shield at half Flesh before their phase break. Telegraph the escalation with shattered columns, an oracle's cry, bronze birds taking flight, or an underworld gate opening.

**Useful terrain:** labyrinth hedges, marble pillars, amphitheater steps, black-water fountains, olive trees, braziers, bronze statues, and broken temples.

These creatures can be stories rather than loot: a Sphinx accepts an answer, Pegasus may choose a worthy rider, and an Empusa can lead champions toward a larger betrayal.

## Ready Arena Bouts

**Labyrinth Under the Stands:** Minotaur Labyrinth-Breaker pursues champions through moving walls while Gorgon Marble-Eye controls sightlines.

**The Black Spring:** Hydra of the Black Spring and Stymphalian Bronze Birds defend poisoned water beneath an old temple.

**Trial of the Golden Hide:** Nemean Lion Cub, Chimera, and a burning ravine arena turn a hunt into a headline bout.

**Gate of the Dead:** Cerberus Pit-Hound guards a shadow gate while Empusa Flame-Shadow and Harpies divide the party.

entities.name: Syncretic Fringe Bestiary — Running Notes
entities.tags: Syncretic Fringe, arena bestiary, running notes
entities.summary: GM guidance for running Syncretic Fringe arena bouts, useful terrain, and ready-made bout hooks for the Greco-Eastern fringe bestiary.
entities.body:
This is a deliberately fictional Asterion fringe where cultural borders blur into threshold magic: crossroads, port cities, ritual scripts, masks, silent rites, sea beacons, and gates between the living and dead. It is not a claim that these traditions were one thing. Standards create pressure, Elites alter information or identity, and Bosses refresh their Spark Shield at half Flesh before a telegraphed phase break.

**Useful terrain:** triple crossroads, harbor quays, mirror wells, processional gates, lighthouse towers, abandoned archives, shrine courts, and painted masks.

Identity and knowledge are central stakes: a creature may demand a name, steal a role, deliver a sealed decree, or offer passage through a dangerous boundary.

## Ready Arena Bouts

**Three Roads, No Return:** Hecatean Threshold Hounds and a Lamia of the Crossroads Well divide the arena into false exits.

**Archive of Winged Ink:** Ibis of the Living Script and Hermetic Bronze Scarabs defend a library whose sentences become walls.

**Beacon at the End of Night:** Pharos Fire-Drake turns a harbor arena into a field of bright, burning signals while Jackal Couriers hunt marked prey.

**Masks Before the High Gate:** Mawu Mask-Thieves serve the Serapis Bull as Harpocrates Silent Wraiths extinguish every command.
